items.title: Are we in for a prolonged pause on interest rates? Some economists think so
items.description: Most experts are tipping interest rates will remain on hold but the question is when will they come down.

items.title: 'Absolutely terrified': Scolyer's doctor reveals fears of experimental therapy
items.description: Just 11 weeks before he died, Richard Scolyer cycled 500km in four days. In his last major TV interview, the celebrated pathologist tells Australian Story the secret to a fulfilling life and his doctor reveals the huge risks he took to try new brain cancer treatment.

items.title: Dream holidays shattered in $4.3 million travel agency collapse
items.description: Australian travellers who collectively lost millions after a travel agency collapsed are calling for an overhaul of consumer protections in the sector.

items.title: Musk's trillions fuelled by AI and his pied piper power over investors
items.description: To get a sense of the difference between the Tesla and SpaceX IPOs, consider that 1.7 billion seconds ago was 1972, when Elton John released Rocket Man, while 1.7 trillion seconds ago was 52,000BC, when we shared the planet with Neanderthals.

items.title: Dashdot customers urged to proceed days before collapse
items.description: Emails and messages seen by ABC News show Dashdot's staff were still encouraging prospective customers to engage with the buyers agency shortly before it entered voluntary liquidation.

items.title: The Socceroos' greatest ever World Cup gamble just paid off
items.description: With his first World Cup team selection, Tony Popovic produced one of the biggest shocks in Socceroos' history. After 90 minutes against Türkiye, his gamble was vindicated.

items.title: Live: Curaçao enjoys magic moment before Germany powers ahead
items.description: World Cup debutant Curaçao enjoys a magical moment in the midst of a drubbing, scoring for the first time in a 7-1 defeat to four-time champion Germany. Follow live.

items.title: Palestinians fear 'archaeology has become a tool' in Israel's plans for West Bank
items.description: Palestinians believe there is more to Israel's recently announced plans to develop heritage sites along the West Bank, arguing archaeology has "become a tool, a mechanism, to justify settlement and justify the displacement of Palestinians" across the area.

items.title: The obscure laws Trump is using to reshape Washington in his image
items.description: Project by project, Donald Trump is altering the United States capital, and in some cases, disrupting views and design that date back more than two centuries.

items.title: Hamilton claims famous Ferrari win, F1 leader suffers late car failure
items.description: Lewis Hamilton has wound back the clock and announced himself as a world championship contender again, claiming his maiden grand prix win as a Ferrari driver.

items.title: Paddleboarder says shark attack victim he helped save was 'very unlucky'
items.description: An off-duty volunteer lifeguard who pulled a woman from the ocean after she was bitten by a shark reveals how he helped save her life while in a state of "panic" himself.

items.title: No Medicare, no family, no visa — these are the babies Australia doesn't count
items.description: For the Pacific Islander women who harvest the fruit and vegetables that stock Australia’s supermarket shelves, motherhood here can mean injury, debt, secrecy and fear.

items.title: Ryan kicks six as Saints get home in GWS thriller at Docklands
items.description: Liam Ryan kicks half a dozen goals as St Kilda earns a thrilling eight-point win over Greater Western Sydney, after Brisbane's victory in Hobart over the Tigers.

items.title: Luai leads Tigers to epic final Leichhardt win
items.description: Jarome Luai has lead the Wests Tigers to a win in their final match at Leichhardt Oval before it's redevelopment.

items.title: New doco charts Rolf Harris's downfall from media king to criminal
items.description: Plus Brisbane is a main character in a new rom-com, Russell T Davies delivers a devastating drama, and we bring you more shows lighting up TV this month.

items.title: History quiz: Test yourself on these past events
items.description: When was Salt Lake City awarded the XIX Winter Olympics? And how much do you know about the Fast and the Furious films? Test yourself in this week's history quiz.

items.title: Rhinos, a river of gold and world domination: This week's Race Around The World
items.description: From dating in Jamaica to world domination in Greenland, catch up on the films from the second week of the new season of Race Around The World.

items.title: Satellite images reveal missing Antarctic ice the 'size of France'
items.description: Scientists say a chunk of winter sea ice the size of France off the Antarctic coast has failed to form this year.

items.title: Tuckwell honours late sister with stunning second place at Dauphiné
items.description: Luke Tuckwell has announced himself as a genuine threat on cycling's world tour, finishing second overall at the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes and dedicated his win to his sister, who passed away last year.

items.title: Police officer in custody after Perth girl shot dead overseas
items.description: A nine-year-old Perth girl has been fatally shot by police in Pakistan after officers mistook her family's car for that of suspected criminals.

items.title: UK armed forces intercept Russian 'shadow fleet' tanker
items.description: The British armed forces have intercepted the sanctioned oil tanker in a bid to disrupt the oil revenue ​that helps fund Russia's war in Ukraine.

items.title: Fair Work rejects gas giant's claim strikes would harm the economy
items.description: One of Australia's biggest gas producers has lost a bid to stop industrial action at its Darwin facilities after claiming strikes would force shutdowns and cause significant damage to the nation's economy.

items.title: Love story: When these childhood friends reunited, the spark was undeniable
items.description: It was a case of puppy love when Cambell first set eyes on Tiana at a Gold Coast housing complex when they were both nine years old. They lost touch when they entered their teens but reunited as adults and have been inseparable since.

items.title: Thousands rally in Belfast to condemn anti-immigrant rioting
items.description: The anti-racism rally came after nights of fiery violence in parts of Northern Ireland following the arrest of a 30-year-old man from Sudan on charges of attempted murder in a stabbing that left a man partly blind.

items.title: African scam victims left homeless in Cambodia amid crackdown
items.description: Hundreds of trafficking survivors from Africa are left stranded in Cambodia amid a widespread crackdown on the country's scam compounds.
